evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/financial.rs:1796,1828,1894 (XLSX renderers render_income_statement_xlsx / render_balance_sheet_xlsx) and :1975,2007 (PDF renderers) all convert monetary figures through f64 with the identical pattern `line.amount.to_string().parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(0.0)` (and `line.balance...` at :1894) before writing them into the exported financial report.

The source fields are exact-precision `Decimal` (confirmed on the accounting/report models in backend/crates/db/src/models — e.g. `pub amount: Decimal`, `pub balance: Decimal`). Round-tripping a Decimal through binary f64 for an income statement / balance sheet reintroduces floating-point representation error into money values that were deliberately kept exact — the class of penny/rounding drift these Decimal columns exist to prevent, now surfacing on the customer-facing PDF/XLSX exports.

The `.unwrap_or(0.0)` fallback is a second, worse defect: if `line.amount.to_string()` ever fails to re-parse as f64, the code silently writes 0.00 into a financial statement instead of erroring. A silent wrong zero in a balance sheet is a data-integrity/correctness failure, not a cosmetic one — the export renders as authoritative with no signal that a line was dropped.

Landable (self-contained backend Rust in financial.rs report renderers, no API/schema change). Fix: format the Decimal directly for the cell (write the value as a string, or serialize via rust_decimal to a fixed 2-dp representation) instead of parsing to f64; and replace `.unwrap_or(0.0)` with propagation of the existing `Result<Vec<u8>, String>` error so an unrenderable amount fails the export rather than becoming a silent 0.00.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/sessions.rs:101 — list_sessions passes query.limit.unwrap_or(50) straight through to the repo. PaginationQuery (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/mod.rs:104-107) declares `limit: Option<i64>` with no bound/validation, so the raw client-supplied value flows to SQL.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/ai_chat.rs:133-163 — list_user_sessions binds the caller-supplied `limit: i64` directly into `LIMIT $2` with NO upper clamp. Same unclamped bind in list_session_messages (ai_chat.rs:223-, `LIMIT $4`) and the third list method (ai_chat.rs:365-, `LIMIT $2`).

Same unclamped `query.limit.unwrap_or(N)` -> repo LIMIT pattern repeats across the whole AI surface with no `.min()` anywhere under routes/ai/: ai/sessions.rs:205,924,997; ai/equipment.rs:203,297,379; ai/voice.rs:308; ai/llm.rs:1448.

Contrast proving this is an oversight, not a convention: admin/users.rs:58 clamps `.min(100)`, admin/audit.rs:235,254 clamp `.min(500)`/`.min(50_000)`, and listing repo backend/crates/db/src/repositories/listing.rs:136 clamps `query.limit.unwrap_or(20).min(100)`. The AI routes are the outlier.

Impact (availability): an authenticated user requesting `?limit=100000000` (limit is i64, up to 9.2e18) forces an unbounded scan + full result-set materialization into memory on the shared pool — slow-query / memory-exhaustion DoS. Landable backend-only fix: clamp at the handler or repo, e.g. `query.limit.unwrap_or(50).min(100)`, mirroring listing.rs:136.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/marketplace.rs:224-289 — search_providers reads `query.limit.unwrap_or(20)` / `query.offset.unwrap_or(0)` (MarketplaceSearchQuery.limit/offset are `Option<i32>`, backend/crates/db/src/models/marketplace.rs:333-335) and string-formats them into `ORDER BY {} {} LIMIT {} OFFSET {}` (marketplace.rs:278) wrapped in `sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql)` — with NO upper clamp on limit.

Route callers pass the raw user-supplied limit unclamped: routes/marketplace.rs:1105, :1252; get_verification_queue at routes/marketplace.rs:1434 -> repo marketplace.rs:1209 (`LIMIT $1`); list_provider_reviews at routes/marketplace.rs:1727 -> repo marketplace.rs:1465 (`LIMIT $2`). None apply `.min()`.

Not an injection: sort_by/sort_order are whitelisted (marketplace.rs:274-286 map to fixed column names / ASC|DESC) and limit/offset are i32 (non-injectable). The defect is availability only — `?limit=2147483647` forces a full scan + large materialization on the marketplace provider-search path (public/authenticated-reachable), a slow-query/memory DoS.
Landable backend-only fix: clamp before the format!/bind, e.g. `let limit = query.limit.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1, 100);`, consistent with the admin/listing repos that already cap.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:311,323,417,427 — all four rentals mutations (createConnection, syncPlatforms, checkIn, checkOut) use the exact same handler: `onError: (error) => handleRentalsAuthError(error, logout)`. That is the ONLY error handling attached to any of them.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:220-226 — handleRentalsAuthError() only reacts to session-loss codes (SESSION_EXPIRED / TOKEN_EXPIRED / TOKEN_INVALID); for every other failure it returns `false` and does nothing. Its own doc comment says 'Non-auth errors are left for the caller to surface' — but the callers ignore the boolean return and surface nothing.

Net effect: a failed check-in / check-out / create-connection / sync-platforms (validation 4xx, backend 5xx, network error) produces ZERO user feedback — no toast, no error state, the button just silently no-ops. The user cannot tell the action failed and may retry blindly or assume success.

Inconsistency proof: the sibling route group frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx:179-185,204-210 does this correctly — its mutation onError handlers call showToast({ type: 'error', ... }) with a t()-wrapped title and the error message. Fix: give the rentals mutations a real onError that, when handleRentalsAuthError returns false, surfaces an error toast (useToast) as financial.tsx does.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:381-383 — BookingsPageRoute wires onCancelBooking, onCheckIn and onCheckOut to `() => {}`. These are live action buttons on the bookings LIST that silently do nothing when clicked.

This is not a not-yet-built stub: the very same check-in / check-out actions ARE implemented as real mutations in BookingDetailPageRoute (rentals.tsx:409-428, rentalsApiCheckIn / rentalsApiCheckOut). So the list-level buttons are dead handlers for functionality that already exists one screen deeper — a genuine wiring gap, not a missing endpoint.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:333-339 (PlatformConnectionsPageRoute onConnect/onDisconnect/onSettings) and :449-456 (BookingDetailPageRoute onEdit/onCancel/onDeleteGuest) are likewise wired to `() => {}` — user-facing buttons that render as functional but perform no action and give no feedback.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx:56-72 — confirmDelete (line 58 `await deleteRule.mutateAsync(deleteConfirm.id)`), handleToggle (line 64 `await updateRule.mutateAsync(...)`) and handleRun (line 71 `await runRule.mutateAsync(rule.id)`) all call mutateAsync with NO try/catch. mutateAsync returns a rejecting promise on failure, so any backend/network error becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

The page never surfaces these mutation errors to the user: grep for updateRule.error / deleteRule.error / runRule.error (and .isError) in the file returns nothing — only the *query* error is rendered ({error} at line 178, from useAutomationRules). So a failed delete/enable-toggle/run silently does nothing on-screen: confirmDelete's `setDeleteConfirm(null)` at line 59 never runs (modal sticks) and the toggle switch visually reverts with no explanation. Contrast EditRulePage.tsx:113 which does render {updateRule.error}. Fix: wrap each handler in try/catch (or use .mutate with onError) and render the mutation error states.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/ExecutionMonitoringPage.tsx:74-77 — handleRetry does `await retryExecution.mutateAsync(log.id); setSelectedLog(null);` with no try/catch. On a failed retry the mutateAsync promise rejects (unhandled rejection) and setSelectedLog(null) never fires, so the details modal stays open with no error shown.

The page surfaces the *query* error (logsError rendered at line 189) but never renders retryExecution.error / retryExecution.isError (grep confirms no such reference), so the retry action has no failure feedback path. Same unhandled-mutation-rejection class as AutomationRulesPage. Fix: try/catch the retry and render retryExecution.error near the retry control.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agent_reviews.rs:190-266 (create_review) validates only `data.rating` (1..=5 at :196) and then binds the free-text `data.body` straight into the `INSERT INTO realtor_reviews (... body ...)` at :255-266 with NO length validation anywhere. CreateReviewRequest.body is `Option<String>` (agent_reviews.rs:47) and there is no MAX_* constant or `.len()` check on it in the whole file (confirmed: grep for body length/cap on this file returns nothing).

This is an authenticated-but-public portal write endpoint (RequestPrincipal, principal_kind = 'public'), i.e. exactly the abuse surface the sibling reality-server endpoints explicitly cap. reports.rs caps its free text at MAX_REPORT_DESCRIPTION_LEN = 5000 (reports.rs:27, enforced at :161) and inquiries.rs caps its message at MAX_INQUIRY_MESSAGE_LEN = 5000 (inquiries.rs:27, enforced at :54 and :446). agent_reviews.rs is the outlier that skipped the same H6 input-hygiene control.

Impact (H6 abuse / resource): a portal user can POST an arbitrarily large review body (bounded only by the global request-body limit, not by an application cap), bloating `realtor_reviews` rows and every log line / response that echoes the review body — the exact unbounded-string abuse the neighboring endpoints were hardened against. The review body is also surfaced back verbatim in list_reviews (:115,:157), amplifying the bloat on every reader.

Landable backend-only fix (self-contained, no API/schema change): add a `const MAX_REVIEW_BODY_LEN: usize = 5000;` and reject over-length `data.body` with 400 before the insert, mirroring reports.rs:161 / inquiries.rs:54. Optionally also reject an all-whitespace/empty body to match the input-hygiene posture of the sibling handlers.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/reports.rs:35 and backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/users.rs:28 each define a byte-for-byte identical private `fn validate_image_or_link_url(s: &str) -> Result<(), String>` (len <= MAX_URL_LEN 2048, then allow only http/https scheme to block stored-XSS `javascript:`/`data:`/`file:` URLs that later render in `` / ``).

Both copies carry an in-code TODO acknowledging the duplication: reports.rs:33-34 ("once the auth-hardening branch lands a shared `url_validator` module this should be swapped for the import") and users.rs:24-25 ("swap for a shared `url_validator` module once it lands on main"). The shared module already exists and is used elsewhere: backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs (validate_fetch_url) is imported by agency_imports.rs:7.

Risk (security-relevant drift): the two copies are an XSS mitigation. If one file's copy is hardened (e.g. also stripping control chars, tightening the scheme list, or normalizing) and the other is not, the profile-image path (users.rs, `profile_image_url` -> ``) or the report-attachment path (reports.rs) silently regresses. Duplicated security predicates diverge under maintenance.

Landable refactor (reality-server only): extract a single scheme/length validator into util/url_validator.rs (alongside the existing validate_fetch_url) and replace both inline copies with the shared import, deleting the two TODOs. No behavior change intended; add one shared unit test covering the reject cases (javascript:/data:/file:, over-length).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 — `fetch(`${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}`)` then `return response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>`: an unvalidated type assertion crossing the API boundary. The parsed body is pushed straight into the comparison context via `addToComparison(result.value)` (lines 59-70) and rendered with no shape validation.

The sibling consumer of the exact same endpoint hardens against this: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:79-89 explicitly comments 'A 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body' and routes every response through `parseListingDetail(body)` before use. ComparisonUrlHandler skips that normalizer, so a truthy-but-malformed 200 (upstream/proxy partial response, wrong-typed fields) is cast to ListingSummary and handed to the comparison UI unchecked.

Severity is bounded (network errors already degrade gracefully via Promise.allSettled at line 54, and the endpoint normally returns a superset ListingDetail), so this is a shape-validation gap rather than a guaranteed crash — but it is a user-facing shared-comparison path that is inconsistent with the codebase's own hardened pattern. Fix: validate/normalize the body (reuse or adapt parseListingDetail / a summary schema guard) before addToComparison, and drop the `as Promise<ListingSummary>` assertion.
